objective: Replace pasted-on rain and make clouds visibly converge/grow into storm banks during a seamless weather transition

changes.rain: Removed all composite screen-grid streaks, sine curtains and spray noise. 120000 analytically advected 3D drops render into the existing HDR/MSAA scene with ocean depth, perspective, shutter length, subpixel energy and environment lighting. No CPU particle simulation or particle buffers.
changes.clouds: Persistent pressure-domain convergence, 1.25→6.25 km cloud depth, 1.5→1 km condensation base, growing bank footprints, 3D billows, multiple-scattering fill, skylight occlusion, adaptive 40m+0.3%-distance steps capped at 448/100km. Erosion filtered as banks mature.
changes.sequence: Heavy rain follows canopy development; drizzle remains independent of deep convection. No image swaps or edited transition crossfades.
changes.distantRain: 16 bounded below-cloud shaft samples use the shared world weather field.

verification.scope: Real native frames from persistent simulation; no image blending/interpolation. Buildup is accelerated; rain-motion is normal speed. Depth override is diagnostic only. Numeric coverage/occlusion gates supplement, not replace, visual review.

reviewed: Depth-tested rain against actual ocean geometry
visualReview.scope: Visual quality assessed from native rendered imagery in addition to numeric gates. The buildup movie is accelerated; the rain movie uses normal physical time.

performance.scope: Sequential unprofiled Apple M1, 1280x800, 180 frames with 60 warmup frames excluded. Storm appearance intentionally changes; before/after are not identical images. No live Ocean preview or concurrent rendering tests; command-buffer times, not energy/WindowServer measurements.

livePreview: Native app reopened once; Weather > Hurricane gradual-transition target verified. Initial hidden/occluded window was paused; presentation through full-screen and back restored a visible, rendering normal window. Night sky/cloud occlusion, rain and changing waves verified visually. Celestial time retained and Follow Local Weather remains available.
limitations: Bounded procedural cloud/rain model rather than a full fluid simulation.
Lightning atmospheric glow/channel remains separate; rain is no longer a composite overlay.
Command-buffer timings do not measure whole-system energy.
